analysis:
Examined all supplied source, patches and mode metadata against the canonical index and selected T-041 detail. ServingReadiness.swift:32-77 adds a diagnostic classification of connection, hold, trust and authorization state; disconnected/untrusted states are blocked, missing status has a 90-second grace, and App Attest currency is delegated to hasCurrentAppAttestAuthorization. Lines 85-164 produce operator advice without executing commands or modifying credentials. No inference, encryption, cache, billing or privileged-helper controls are changed in this implementation. ProviderLogger.swift:147-149 adds only fixed operational messages; existing private handling of free-form strings remains intact, with no new prompt, token or stable-identity exposure (A-001, A-008, T-058).
ProviderLoop+Capacity.swift:82 (head patch) now invokes superviseServingAuthorization after asynchronous capacity/model maintenance and before writing state. Its implementation is absent here, so recovery/re-registration safety cannot be established from the message text. Integration should examine its idle/inflight guards, cooldowns, connection-generation binding and grant invalidation (A-018, T-053, T-057), including whether preceding awaits can delay supervision. Also verify that connection changes clear stale daemon trust and that ServingReadiness's hardware-without-authorization and legacy-path verdicts at lines 58-68 match the actual wire contract and remain diagnostic-only (T-052, T-053, T-058). These are unverified cross-file contracts, not demonstrated missing controls. No independently supported security regression qualifies in this local scope.
